column3: The early palace of the Qing emperors before they moved to Beijing, with a mix of Manchu, Han and Mongol styles, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The mansion of the warlord Zhang Zuolin and his son Zhang Xueliang, a grand compound with Chinese and Western buildings.
A large park with the tomb of Hong Taiji, the second Qing emperor, among old pines and a lake.
The oldest pedestrian shopping street in China, with old shops, department stores, and snack stalls in Shenyang.
Fuling is the tomb of Nurhaci, the founder of the Qing, in a forested park on a hill outside Shenyang.
A museum with famous scrolls and paintings, as well as the treasures of the Liao dynasty and local archaeology.
A dumpling house with a history of nearly 200 years in Shenyang, known for its dumplings, which are fried first and then steamed.
Crispy slices of pork coated in a sweet and sour sauce, a signature dish of the northeast.
A winter stew of sauerkraut, glass noodles and pork, hot and tangy and a cold-weather comfort dish.
Skewers of lamb, beef and vegetables grilled over charcoal, a Shenyang summer night staple.
A halal shaomai, with a thin wrapper and juicy beef or lamb filling, a Shenyang specialty for over a century.
Roasted chicken frames are a street snack of Shenyang, crisp outside, and eaten with beer.
A comic song-and-dance duet from the northeast, with humor, bright costumes and a lot of improvisation.
An opera that began in northern China in the early 20th century, with simple, accessible tunes and stories of ordinary life.
A folk dance of the northeast, performed in groups in bright costumes with fans and handkerchiefs.
One of the largest city squares in the world, by the sea in Dalian, with a huge compass pattern in the paving.
A seaside park with aquariums, polar animals and a cable car, on the coast of Dalian.
A long coastline of strange rocks, cliffs and beaches shaped by the sea, near Dalian.
A historic naval port at the tip of the Liaodong Peninsula, with old forts and a role in the wars of the early 20th century.
A major port on the Yellow Sea, one of the busiest in northern China.
A scenic road along the coast of Dalian, with sea views, cliffs and parks.
Dalian's restaurants serve sea cucumber, scallops, prawns and abalone fresh from the Yellow Sea, with simple steaming or stir-frying.
A jelly made from sweet potato starch, fried and served with garlic sauce. It is a classic Dalian snack.
Dumplings with a filling of shrimp, fish and vegetables, a popular choice in Dalian.
Seafood and meat grilled over charcoal on Dalian's streets, with a strong taste of the sea.
A garden with a huge Buddha carved from a single piece of jade from nearby Xiuyan.
A mountain of granite peaks, temples and Buddhist monasteries, known as the Pearl of the Northeast.
Round pies, pan-fried until golden, with a juicy meat filling, from Haicheng.
A green jade from Xiuyan, carved into pendants, bowls and Buddha statues.
A memorial museum to Lei Feng, a soldier who became a symbol of selfless service, with displays of his life and diary.
A craft that carves a shiny black stone, coal amber, into small animals and ornaments.
A bridge across the Yalu River that was bombed during the Korean War, half of it still stands.
The eastern end of the Ming Great Wall, which climbs a hill beside the Yalu River, facing North Korea.
Dandong is known for sweet, large strawberries, picked in spring and often given as gifts.
A yellow clam from the Yellow Sea, steamed or stir-fried, a fresh and sweet seafood of Dandong.
Grilled meat skewers served with a special dip, and a popular dinner tradition in Jinzhou.
Crunchy pickled vegetables from Jinzhou, served as a side dish or a snack.
A large, savory flatbread from Yingkou, baked until golden and eaten with soup or meat.
Fuxin is known for its agate, carved into small ornaments and sold as a local craft.
An octagonal pagoda from the Liao dynasty, standing tall in Liaoyang, with carved Buddha figures on each level.
In autumn, a vast tidal flat on the coast turns bright red with sea-blite plants. A boardwalk lets you walk over the red carpet.
River crabs from the rice paddies of Panjin, which are famous for their sweet meat and are in season in autumn.
A wetland with lotus flowers, reed beds and birds, a quiet place near Tieling.
Hazelnuts from the hills near Tieling, a popular snack with a sweet and rich taste.
A hill in Chaoyang with temples and old pagodas, and a long history of worship.
A Ming-dynasty walled town on the coast, with intact walls and gates, and a rare example of a fully walled old town.
Seafood from the Bohai Sea, simply cooked in the seaside restaurants of Xingcheng.
Jellyfish from the Bohai Sea, cut into strips and served as a cold dish with vinegar and sesame oil.
One of the largest water caves in the world, where you float by boat through a long underground river among glowing stalactites.
A scenic mountain with maple forests that blaze red in autumn, and a river valley with cliffs.
A small wild mountain grape, sour and sweet, used for juice and wine.
